1.explanation:
1. Pagination.js (React): This is where the `pageSizes` prop is declared as `arrayOf(number)`, the dropdown is built via `pageSizes.map(size => <SelectItem value={size} text={String(size)} />)`, and the selected size is parsed via `Number(evt.target.value)`. To support objects with separate `value` and `text`, this file needs to accept a new shape in propTypes, branch on object vs. number, render `<SelectItem value={size.value} text={size.text} />` when appropriate, and stop coercing to Number incorrectly.
2. Pagination-test.js: All existing tests assume `pageSizes` is an array of numbers and that the text of each `SelectItem` is `String(size)`. These tests will need to be updated (or new tests added) to verify that passing objects with `{value,text}` renders the custom label and preserves correct range calculations.
3. Pagination-story.js: The Storybook knobs currently treat `pageSizes` as a simple array of numbers. To demo the new feature, the story definition must be updated to accept and display an array of objects, e.g. via a JSON knob or a custom control shape, so that authors can supply `{value: 100, text: 'All'}` entries in the live Playground.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshots show that when a developer adds a custom “All” option to `pageSizes` (e.g. `{value: totalItems, text: 'All'}`), the pagination UI renders “Items per page All” but the item-range and page-count labels break: “NaN–NaN of 200 items” and “of NaN pages.” Because the component only ever treated `pageSizes` as numbers (mapping each size to `String(size)` and coercing `evt.target.value` to `Number`), passing an object leads to arithmetic on an object (→ NaN) and the wrong `text` in the dropdown.
